source.title: Meta-analytic evidence for common and distinct neural networks associated with directly experienced pain and empathy for pain.

confidence_rationale: Image-based (9 studies) and coordinate-based (32 studies) meta-analysis confirms a reliable anterior insula / anterior-midcingulate core shared between first-hand pain and empathy for pain, consistent with routing through own affective machinery. Held at 0.6 because overlap in fMRI is not identity of representation, and the meta-analysis itself shows paradigm-dependent recruitment of mentalizing (TPJ, vmPFC, precuneus) or action-understanding regions, i.e. more than the self stream is involved.
failure_signatures: Spatial overlap at fMRI resolution can reflect distinct but intermixed populations or domain-general salience/negative-affect responses rather than a shared suffering representation.
Paradigm-dependence (cue-based vs picture-based) means 'empathy for pain' is not one mechanism; the shared-core reading applies best to the affective component.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A core network of bilateral anterior insula and medial/anterior cingulate is associated with empathy for pain and overlaps with directly experienced pain; depending on paradigm it co-activates with action-understanding regions (picture-based) or mentalizing regions (abstract cue-based); only picture-based paradigms recruit somatosensory cortex.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the claim that other-bound affect reuses the agent's own affective (not sensory) streams: the shared core is the affective/interoceptive component, matching MECH-405's choice of SD-011 suffering and MECH-112 wanting rather than sensory channels. The paradigm-dependent add-ons map onto the other-model slot (mentalizing) and ARC-010 mirror modelling (action understanding).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Co-activation evidence only. The distinct networks are as informative as the shared core: they indicate that the 'binding' part of the claim is carried by separate machinery whose contribution varies with cue type, which the claim text does not currently acknowledge.
mapping.source_context: Image-based and coordinate-based fMRI meta-analysis of empathy-for-pain studies (includes the Singer et al. 2004 Science loved-one paradigm lineage).

confidence_components.notes: Solid meta-analysis; mapping limited by correlational overlap; affective-not-sensory split maps well onto the claim's choice of streams.
